title: Add sealed-audit-headers and KMS origin policy evaluator
author: Nora Patel
description: Motivation: Customers operating under regional data residency and custodial key constraints need guarantees that (1) audit metadata cannot be injected or replayed by downstream services and (2) KMS key usage is provably tied to allowed key origins. This PR introduces two complementary controls: (A) sealed-audit-headers: an immutable header envelope added at the edge (gateway) and verified by services and the audit-forwarder before logs are persisted or exported; (B) kms-origin-policy-evaluator: a policy plugin in the request-authorizer that rejects crypto-ops when the requested key origin region is not allowed for the tenant. Together these reduce risk of accidental cross-region key usage and audit tampering. Changes: 1) gateway: add sealing middleware that computes a signature over canonical audit headers and a request nonce, emits X-Redwood-Audit-Seal and X-Redwood-Audit-Seal-V:1 and rejects requests that present non-matching unsealed audit headers. 2) authorizer: new kms_origin_policy evaluator consulted by RBAC v2 policy engine; policy predicate 'kms_origin in allowed_regions' implemented and configurable per-tenant. 3) audit-forwarder: extended to validate sealed headers before forwarding to external SIEM and to include origin verification metadata in exported envelopes. 4) rbac-mapping: new service-account -> tenant binding validator to prevent service accounts from being used across tenant boundaries for KMS ops. 5) docs and console: admin UI surfaces to view tenants' allowed KMS regions and compliance status. Implementation notes: sealed header uses HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped signing key stored in KMS; signature computed on a deterministic ordering of audit headers plus request id and timestamp window to prevent replay. Policy evaluator consults tenant metadata and falls back to explicit deny when metadata missing; rollout flag 'security.kms_enforce_origin' gate controls evaluator. Tests: unit tests for header canonicalization, property-based tests for canonical ordering, integration test harness exercising gateway->authorizer->audit-forwarder path with both permitted and denied key origins, e2e smoke in staging using synthetic tenant configs. Backwards compatibility: if gate is off, system behaves as before; gateway accepts requests without seals but emits advisory log so operators can estimate impact. Migration: a lightweight migration adds tenant.allowed_kms_regions string array and a signing_key_reference to the tenants table; an offline job (scripts/migrations/73199-populate-tenant-kms) prepared to backfill likely values from billing metadata but requires manual review for ambiguous tenants. Security review: SEC reviewed the design and requested sealed header TTL of 90s and replay nonce store eviction policy; these are implemented. Rollout plan: enable in canary region for 48h, monitor audit-forwarder rejects metric and application 403 spikes, then progressively enable with config locks per-account. Related: ENG-1157 explains the policy schema, SUP-934 contains a customer support case that motivated origin enforcement.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice design. Please add explicit tests for header ordering; I want to be sure no accidental canonicalization drift occurs.
Author (Nora Patel): Added property-based tests and a test vector file with canonical ordering examples.
Li Wei: What is the performance impact on p99 for the authorizer path? Can we cache policy decisions per-request-id?
Author (Nora Patel): Benchmarked in perf-canary: median auth path +1.8ms, p99 +3.2ms at 10k rps due to HMAC; added a short in-memory cache with 15s TTL to mitigate repeated header rechecks behind LB.
Ava Thompson: We need a migration rollback plan if tenant backfill assigns a wrong region. Add a manual remediation doc.
Author (Nora Patel): Added remediation steps in docs and a dry-run flag for the backfill script.
merge_details: post-merge-note: feature gate 'security.kms_enforce_origin' is off by default; ops to enable per-region
release_notes: Add immutable sealed audit headers to protect audit metadata from injection and a KMS origin policy evaluator to enforce tenant allowed key regions. Configurable via feature gate security.kms_enforce_origin. Requires tenant metadata migration (tenant.allowed_kms_regions).
notes_for_ops: Canary plan: enable in us-west-2 for 48h before wider rollout
Rollback: flip security.kms_enforce_origin=false and disable gateway seal enforcement if needed
